subject: Re: Metering proxy & entitlement routing for AWS Marketplace SaaS integration
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@dataslate.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Metering granularity + entitlement proxy question for AWS SaaS listing

Hey Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're getting ready to list on AWS Marketplace and are trying to lock the right metering surface so our finance and ops teams can reconcile downstream. A couple of constraints on our side: 
- We have two SKUs (Standard / Enterprise) with overlapping feature flags but shared tenant IDs.
- We plan to route some usage through a centralized proxy (ingest cluster) that reports consumption to AWS metering APIs on behalf of tenants.
- We need per-tenant entitlements in our billing system but want to avoid per-tenant marketplace subscriptions.

Specific asks: can Redwood support a proxying pattern where a single marketplace SaaS contract + multiple internal entitlements map to per-tenant seats/consumption? What are recommended fallback flows when the AWS metering service is delayed or returns 5xx? Also need a sample mapping file we can use to map Marketplace SKU -> internal entitlement_id -> invoice SKU.

Can you share a short runbook and the risks we should raise to procurement/legal? We're targeting a limited GA on May 10, so timeline is tight.

Best,
Laura Chen
VP, Platform
Dataslate Analytics

--
Attachments: initial-usage-sample.csv (referenced)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@dataslate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metering granularity + entitlement proxy question for AWS SaaS listing

Hi Laura — great summary, and thanks for the clear timeline. Short answer: yes, the proxying pattern is supported but there are trade-offs and a recommended canonical mapping we use in production. I attached a diagram and a starter CSV for the mapping. Key points up front:

- Single marketplace contract + internal entitlements: we map the Marketplace SKU (contract level) to one or more internal entitlement_ids. The runtime emits a Marketplace metering call for the aggregate contract usage while our billing system applies the entitlement-level allocation. This avoids forcing per-tenant Marketplace subscriptions.

- Metering proxy behavior: Redwood's SDK supports an asynchronous emit with durable local queueing + exponential backoff. We recommend batching at sub-second boundaries for cost efficiency and to reduce pressure on the AWS Metering API. If AWS returns 5xx, the runtime retries with jitter; if the outage persists beyond your SLO window, configure an offline-claim mode where we persist delta usage to your S3 bucket and reconcile once services recover.

- Reconciliation & audit: include an ordered mapping file (attached) with immutable mapping ids, and push daily reconciliation reports (signed hashes) to a shared S3 prefix. That protects both sides during dispute windows.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) for the next 4 weeks:
1) This week: Ben & Karthik review the mapping CSV and validate Marketplace SKU -> internal SKU mapping (owner: Ben).
2) Next week: Marissa to draft a canary runbook and S3 prefix layout for delta claims + reconciliation (owner: Marissa).
3) Week of Apr 23: Test canary — 3 tenants on the proxy path, validate end-to-end metering events into AWS, and run reconciliation.
4) Week of May 6: Final contract sign-off, DocuSign route, and production flip on May 10.

Risks to flag for procurement/legal:
- Contract language around delayed metering / usage adjustments and the window for claims.
- Required evidence: daily signed reconciliation files, request/response logs for disputed hours.
- Data residency: if you plan to keep delta files in a different region we need to ensure the contract reflects that.

I attached: entitlement-proxy-diagram.pdf, metering-mapping-v1.csv, redwood-saas-fulfillment-checklist.xlsx. Also linking a short runbook draft: https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-runbooks/dataslate-metering-canary.md

Ben/Karthik/Marissa: can you confirm owners and any missing dependencies?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: entitlement-proxy-diagram.pdf (2.1MB), metering-mapping-v1.csv (3KB), redwood-saas-fulfillment-checklist.xlsx (42KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura@dataslate.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metering granularity + entitlement proxy question for AWS SaaS listing

Laura / team — I reviewed the mapping CSV and did a quick inventory against our standard invoice SKU set. Proposed adjustments in the attached file: we need an explicit "reconciliation_sku" column so that finance can ingest reconciled deltas without touching contract SKUs.

Quick timeline confirmation from my side:
- Ben to produce updated mapping (owner: Ben) by Apr 13.
- Karthik to add the fulfillment webhook spec (owner: Karthik) by Apr 16.
- Marissa to publish the canary runbook and grant Dataslate access to the S3 prefix by Apr 18.

I'll also open a HubSpot deal note and add the DocuSign routing once Marissa confirms the final contract language. DocuSign skeleton: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABCD-1234

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment referenced: metering-mapping-v1-reviewed.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@dataslate.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metering granularity + entitlement proxy question for AWS SaaS listing

Thanks all — jumping in with the runbook details and access plan.

I pushed a canary runbook to the shared S3 link (see above) and created an IAM role template for Dataslate to assume for the canary tests (least privilege: write to s3://dataslate-metering-canary/ and put-object for reconciliation). Please note: we will not enable automatic invoice adjustments until reconciliation hash verification passes for 7 consecutive days. That should be an explicit contract clause.

Forwarding the checklist and including the typical fallback play: if the AWS Metering endpoint is degraded for >2 hours, the proxy will flip to offline mode and persist events to your region bucket. Redwood will surface an incident that triggers a manual reconciliation run and, if necessary, a temporary credit hold. We should convert this into a short clause for procurement: a 30-day dispute window with a signed daily reconciliation file as primary evidence.

Laura — next steps for you: share the initial three tenant IDs for the canary and confirm the S3 prefix you'd like. I can add Dataslate's AWS account to the IAM role once you confirm.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
